question: Do the green claims in the prospectus and ISS second-party opinion hold up against the loan tape, and are the CFP impact figures consistent?

plan.explanation: To answer whether green claims in the prospectus and ISS second-party opinion hold up against the loan tape, and whether CFP impact figures are consistent, we need to: (1) load the prospectus and extract its green claims, (2) load the ISS second-party opinion (investor_report is the closest available PDF — but actually the context only has prospectus, investor_report, and loan_tape; the ISS SPO is not listed, so we use the investor_report as the second green-claims document), (3) load the loan tape, (4) test each document's green claims against the loan tape via analyzer.claim_vs_collateral, and (5) compare the green definitions/claims between the two documents via analyzer.definition_comparator. This gives a cited, verified answer with minimum steps.

Notes as "green bond"  
The Secured Green Collateralised Notes are intended to be aligned with the Green Bond Principles, as 'Secured Green Collateral Bond' as defined in the Green Bond Principles in effect as 
at the date of this Prospectus. The Green Bond Principles are voluntary process guidelines that include four core components: (i) use of proceeds, (ii) process for project evaluation and 
selection, (iii) management of proceeds and (iv) reporting. The Green Bond Principles are further described in Section 6.6 (Green Bond Principles and Energy Performance Certificates). 
The Secured Green Collateralised Notes are not a "European green bond" or "EuGB" under the EUGBS Regulation and do not comply with the requirements set out therein. Each of the 
Mortgage Receivables (including those relating to Mortgage Loans where part of the loan comprises a Construction Deposit) will be required to meet, among other things, the Eligibility 
Criteria and the Green Eligibility Criteria as at the relevant Transfer Date of such Mortgage Receivable, meaning, in relation to the Initial Portfolio, the Initial Cut-Off Date and, in relation 
to Mortgage Loans under which New Mortgage Receivables arise, the relevant Cut-Off Date. In order to seek alignment with Article 3 of the EU Taxonomy Regulation, including by virtue 
of alignment with the EU Taxonomy TSC building requirement, the Green Eligibility Criteria require that the Mortgaged Asset, on which the relevant Mortgage Loan from which such 
Mortgage Receivable arises is secured, is assigned: (1) if it is built before 1 January 2021: a definitive Energy Performance Certificate of at least, "A" (based on an energy performance 
demand determination method prescribed or permitted under applicable legislation at the relevant time that the Energy Performance Certificate was issued or otherwise referred to in the 
Energy Performance Certificate, whereby (information in respect of) the most recent Energy Performance Certificate available to the Seller on the relevant Cut-Off Date shall be used to

demand (PED) of: (i) 27kWh/m2 per year if the Mortgaged Asset is a residential house (woning) or (ii) 45kWh/m2 per year if the Mortgaged Asset is a residential apartment (appartement) 
(in each case based on an energy performance determination method prescribed or permitted under applicable legislation at the relevant time that the Energy Performance Certificate was

accordance with Article 27 of the EU Securitisation Regulation, confirming that the requirements of Articles 19 to 22 of the EU Securitisation Regulation for designation as EU STS

ESMA, will be available for download on the ESMA STS Register website at https://www.esma.europa.eu/policy-activities/securitisation/simple-transparent-and-standardised-sts-
securitisation (or its successor website) (the "ESMA STS Register Website"). For the avoidance of doubt, the ESMA STS Register Website and the contents thereof do not form part of

The Secured Green Collateralised Notes are intended to be aligned with the Green Bond Principles, as 'Secured Green Collateral Bond' as defined in the Green Bond Principles in effect as 
at the date of this Prospectus. The Green Bond Principles are voluntary process guidelines that include four core components: (i) use of proceeds, (ii) process for project evaluation and 
selection, (iii) management of proceeds and (iv) reporting. The Green Bond Principles are further described in Section 6.6 (Green Bond Principles and Energy Performance Certificates). 
The Secured Green Collateralised Notes are not a "European green bond" or "EuGB" under the EUGBS Regulation and do not comply with the requirements set out therein. Each of the

definitions_a.definition: The EU Taxonomy Regulation indicator for the energy performance of a building, expressed in the Netherlands as the BENG 2 indicator (maximum allowed usage of primary fossil energy per square meter on an annual basis), used to assess whether newly constructed buildings meet the nearly zero energy building criteria.
definitions_a.excerpt: The EU Taxonomy Regulation sets the Primary Energy Demand (PED) as an indicator for the energy performance of a building. The EU Taxonomy Regulation requires newly constructed buildings to be built according to the nearly zero energy building (NZEB) criteria and the PED should be 10% less than the locally applicable threshold value. In The Netherlands PED is expressed as the BENG 2 indicator and for new constructions a threshold value is calculated, recorded and published.

assessments.rationale: All 3,237 loans carry an EPC label drawn from the A-family (A, A+, A++, A+++, A++++) with only 2 rated C and 1 Unknown, confirming that EPC labels expressed as letters between A and G are present and recorded across the pool as described.

A primary_energy_demand_kwh_m2 field is populated for all 3,237 loans with a mean of 72.41 kWh/m² and a range of -112 to 231 kWh/m², consistent with the BENG 2 indicator being used to capture primary fossil energy demand per square metre annually.

The vast majority of loans show EPC labels of A or better and a mean PED of 72.41 kWh/m², but 2 loans carry a C label and 1 is Unknown, and the maximum PED of 231 kWh/m² materially exceeds the 27/45 kWh/m² thresholds for post-2020 buildings, indicating that not all loans demonstrably satisfy the stated green eligibility criteria.

The loan tape provides only mean PED (72.41 kWh/m²) and no CO2-emission figures, reference-group benchmarks, or total-pool emission calculations, so the specific claims of 5,761 tons/year reduction and 36.3% improvement cannot be verified from the available data.

The loan tape contains no CO2-emission field or reference-group comparison data; while EPC labels and PED values are present, they are insufficient on their own to verify the portfolio-level carbon footprint figures cited in the CFP Portfolio Emissions Report.

While most loans show A-or-better EPC labels and EPCs issued between 2021 and 2026 (mean 2024), the presence of 2 C-rated loans, 1 Unknown, and a maximum PED of 231 kWh/m² well above the 27/45 kWh/m² post-2020 thresholds raises doubt that every loan in the pool meets the stated green eligibility criteria.

EU Taxonomy sustainability requires assessment of Do No Significant Harm criteria, minimum social safeguards, and technical screening criteria beyond energy performance, none of which can be evaluated from the EPC label, PED, and construction deposit fields available in the loan tape.
